title: Instance search ran out of heartbeats
explanation: Typeclass synthesis hit its own budget (`synthInstance.maxHeartbeats`, 20000 by default) before finding an instance. Often a general instance is tried early and starts a long search that fails.
fixes: If the search can succeed but is long, raise the budget for this declaration only: `set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 200000 in`, with a comment that says why.
Demote the instance that leads the search astray: `attribute [local instance 20] Foo.toBar` (find it with `set_option trace.Meta.synthInstance true in`).
Provide the instance directly with `haveI`/`letI`, or add a shortcut `instance : C T := inferInstance` once.
example: (deterministic) timeout at `synthInstance`, maximum number of heartbeats (20000) has been reached

title: Instance problem too large (synthInstance.maxSize)
explanation: The instance terms grew past the size limit, typically with deeply nested index types (sums of sums, products of matrix types) or long chains of structure projections.
fixes: Raise the limit for the one declaration: `set_option synthInstance.maxSize 512 in` (the default is 128), with a comment naming the nested types.
Name the nested type with an `abbrev` or a `def` with its own instances, so the search sees a small term.
Check that the instance exists at all (`#synth`), since a missing instance also fails, only later.
example:
failed to synthesize
  Fintype ((m ⊕ n) ⊕ (p ⊕ q))
maximum class-instance resolution size has been reached

title: Timeout while unifying (definitions being unfolded)
explanation: The defeq checker is unfolding definitions such as `Finset.sum`, `Finset.univ` or a large construction while comparing two terms, often in `exact`, `rw` or `apply`.
fixes: Seal the definitions for this declaration: `seal Finset.sum Finset.prod Finset.univ in` before the lemma (or `seal myBigDef in`).
Elaborate the term before unifying with the goal: `exact (foo h :)` instead of `exact foo h`.
Make large definitions irreducible after proving their API lemmas: `attribute [irreducible] myDef`.
example: (deterministic) timeout at `isDefEq`, maximum number of heartbeats (200000) has been reached

pattern: maximum recursion depth has been reached|simp failed, maximum number of steps exceeded
title: simp loops between a lemma and its reverse
explanation: A simp set contains a lemma together with a lemma that undoes it (for example `foo` and `← foo_assoc`), or a definition is unfolded and refolded, so simp never terminates.
fixes: Leave one direction out: `simp [-foo, ← foo]` or remove the reversed lemma from the list.
Use `simp only [...]` with an explicit list, and mark lemmas that must act first as pre-lemmas: `simp [↓map_mul]`.
If a default simp lemma always misleads, erase it for the file with `attribute [-simp] foo`.
example:
maximum recursion depth has been reached
use `set_option maxRecDepth <num>` to increase limit

pattern: motive is not type correct|did not find instance of the pattern.*(decidable|Decidable|Fintype)
title: Rewrite fails on a different Decidable or Fintype instance
explanation: The goal and the lemma carry different (non-defeq) instances, for example the classical `DecidableEq` against a computing one, or `Fintype.ofFinite` against `Fin n`'s own instance, so the pattern does not match syntactically.
fixes: Bridge the instances with `convert h using 2`, `congr!`, or a small `@[simp]` lemma proved by `congr` (instances of `Decidable`/`Fintype` are subsingletons).
Put `open scoped Classical in` on the definition instead of the whole file, and add `Fintype.ofFinite` only as `attribute [local instance low]`.
State results with `Nat.card` instead of `Fintype.card` to avoid the instance altogether.
example: tactic 'rewrite' failed, motive is not type correct
